fields.title: Stomach cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Stomach cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Stomach cancer is a serious condition that requires prompt, accurate diagnosis and a comprehensive approach to treatment. Israeli clinics offer some of the most advanced methods of diagnosing and treating stomach cancer, combining innovative medical technology with highly qualified specialists.

Diagnosis of stomach cancer

  1. Endoscopy (gastroscopy)
    The main diagnostic method, allowing the doctor to examine the inner surface of the stomach and take tissue samples (a biopsy) for histological examination.
  2. Biopsy
    Examination of tissue samples for an accurate diagnosis.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. Laboratory tests
    These include blood tests, checks for tumour markers and other specific tests that may indicate stomach cancer.
  4. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    Provide detailed images that can reveal the presence of a tumour, its size and extent.
  5. PET-CT
    A highly informative method for assessing the metabolic activity of the tumour and identifying metastases.

Treatment of stomach cancer

  1. Surgery
    The main treatment, involving partial or total gastrectomy (removal of the stomach), often with removal of some of the lymph nodes.
  2. Chemotherapy
    Used both before and after the operation to destroy cancer cells, and as the main treatment for patients with metastatic cancer.
  3. Radiotherapy
    Used in combination with chemotherapy to shrink the tumour before an operation or to destroy any remaining cancer cells afterwards.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    The newest treatments, directed at specific molecular targets in the tumour and at stimulating the immune system to fight the cancer.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach
    Israel's leading clinics use a team approach to treatment, providing a comprehensive assessment and an individual treatment strategy for every patient.
  • Innovative treatments
    Patients have access to the latest advances in oncology, including targeted therapy and immunotherapy, all of which considerably improves the chances of successful treatment.
  • Highly qualified specialists
    Oncologists, surgeons, radiologists and other specialists in Israel have international experience and regularly exchange knowledge with colleagues from other countries.
  • Quality and comfort of treatment
    Israeli medical centres provide a high standard of medical care and comfort. Considerable attention is given not only to patients' physical but also to their psychological condition, with support at every stage of treatment.
  • Access to clinical trials
    Patients have the opportunity to take part in international clinical trials of the newest medicines and therapies, which gives access to innovative treatments not yet available in other countries.
  • Individualised treatment programmes
    Every patient is given a personalised treatment plan that takes account of the features of their illness, their general health and their personal preferences and goals. This makes treatment as effective as possible while minimising the risk of side effects.

Choosing Israel for the treatment of stomach cancer gives patients access to world-class medical care, combining advanced technology, highly qualified medical specialists and a whole-person approach to the health of every patient.

fields.title: Sarcoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Treatment and diagnosis of sarcoma in Israel

Sarcoma is a rare and complex disease that requires a comprehensive approach to diagnosis and treatment. Thanks to their experience, advanced technology and individual approach to every patient, Israeli medical centres offer some of the most effective ways of fighting this disease.

Diagnosis of sarcoma

  1. The start of the process
    physical examination and medical history. Doctors begin with a detailed full medical history and a physical examination. After that, on the basis of the initial findings, the doctor decides what further investigations are needed.
  2. Laboratory tests
    The key laboratory tests are a full blood count and blood biochemistry. A full blood count can reveal changes characteristic of cancer. Blood biochemistry helps assess the working of various organs and systems, including the liver and kidneys, which is important for a complete picture of the patient's health.
  3. PET-CT (positron emission tomography)
    This method is used to assess the metabolic activity of the tumour and identify metastases at an early stage. It allows the position of the tumour to be established precisely and the effectiveness of treatment to be assessed.
  4. Biopsy
    This procedure involves taking tumour tissue for histological analysis, which is the key method for establishing the type of sarcoma. A biopsy is needed for definitive confirmation of the diagnosis and for choosing a treatment strategy. Histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed.

After analysing all the results, the professor will establish the diagnosis and prescribe the appropriate treatment. It is worth noting that the diagnostic process itself takes up to 3 working days.

Treatments for sarcoma

  1. Surgery
    The main aim is complete removal of the tumour while preserving healthy tissue. Depending on the position and size of the sarcoma, reconstructive surgery may be required.
  2. Radiotherapy
    Given before or after the operation to destroy any remaining cancer cells or to shrink the tumour before surgery.
  3. Chemotherapy
    This method is used to destroy cancer cells throughout the body. It may be given before or after an operation, or as the main treatment for certain types of sarcoma.
  4. Targeted therapy
    It is directed at particular genetic or molecular targets found in the cancer cells.
  5. Immunotherapy
    This treatment stimulates the body's immune system to fight the cancer and is particularly effective in certain types of sarcoma.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of sarcoma

  • Advanced medical technology. Israeli clinics are equipped with the most modern devices.
  • Experienced specialists. Israel is home to leading experts in oncology who have extensive experience in treating sarcoma.
  • An individual approach. Every patient is given a personalised treatment plan.
  • Reasonable prices. Prices for treatment in Israel are competitive, and the quality of medical care fully matches the cost. This makes treatment accessible to a wide range of patients from all over the world.
  • High patient satisfaction. Thanks to the quality of the service and the attention to detail, patients feel both confident and comfortable at every stage of treatment, and — importantly — there is no language barrier.

In choosing Israel, patients receive not only treatment to the highest world standards but also care and support at every stage of their journey to recovery.

fields.title: Multiple sclerosis
fields.bodyHtml:
Multiple sclerosis: innovative treatment in Israel

Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic disease of the central nervous system characterised by damage to the myelin sheath of the nerve fibres. This can lead to a wide range of symptoms, including fatigue, poor coordination, problems with vision and many others. Israel is one of the leading centres for the treatment of MS, giving patients access to innovative methods of diagnosis and therapy.

Diagnosis of multiple sclerosis in Israel:

  1. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    The main method of diagnosing MS, allowing areas of demyelination in the brain and spinal cord to be detected.
  2. Laboratory tests
    For the detection of oligoclonal IgG.
  3. Examination of the cerebrospinal fluid (lumbar puncture)
    Helps detect changes characteristic of MS, including the presence of oligoclonal bands.
  4. Neurological examination: Assessment of the functions of the central nervous system and identification of disturbances in nerve conduction.

Treatments for multiple sclerosis:

  1. Disease-modifying therapy
    Medicines that slow the progression of the disease and reduce the frequency of relapses. Both traditional and the newest medicines are available in Israel.
  2. Treatment of relapses
    A course of high-dose corticosteroids, usually given intravenously, to reduce inflammation and speed recovery.
  3. Symptomatic treatment
    Prescribed to ease particular symptoms such as fatigue, spasticity, bladder problems and others.
  4. Rehabilitation
    Includes physiotherapy, therapeutic exercise, occupational therapy and speech therapy to maintain physical activity and improve quality of life.
  5. Psychological support
    Psychotherapy and support groups for patients and their families.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A personalised approach: Treatments are chosen individually according to the form of MS, the stage of the disease and the patient's general condition.
  • Innovative treatments: The opportunity to take part in clinical trials of new medicines and therapies.
  • A multidisciplinary team: Leading specialists in neurology, rehabilitation and psychotherapy work together to achieve the best results.

Treatment of multiple sclerosis in Israel aims to slow the progression of the disease as far as possible, reduce symptoms and improve patients' quality of life.

fields.title: Retinoblastoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Retinoblastoma is a malignant tumour of the retina of the eye. It is a rare condition, but it is the most common cancer inside the eye in children. If left untreated, retinoblastoma can lead to loss of sight and to the spread of cancer cells to other parts of the body.

Diagnosis of retinoblastoma

  1. Detailed review of the medical history:
    • The doctor gathers information about symptoms such as a white reflex in the pupil, squint, and pain or redness of the eyes, and also considers the family history of the condition.
  2. Visual examination and ophthalmoscopy:
    • The ophthalmologist examines the fundus with an ophthalmoscope to identify a tumour in the retina.
  3. Ultrasound examination of the eye:
    • An ultrasound of the eye helps image the internal structures of the eye and establish the size and position of the tumour.
  4. Computed tomography (CT):
    • A CT scan helps obtain detailed images of the eye and identify any spread of the tumour beyond it.
  5. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    • MRI is used for a more precise study of the soft tissues of the eye and to identify metastases.
  6. Fluorescein angiography:
    • This method allows the blood supply to the retina to be assessed and abnormalities associated with the tumour to be identified.
  7. Genetic testing:
    • Carried out to establish whether mutations are present in the RB1 gene, which are associated with the hereditary form of retinoblastoma.

Treatment of retinoblastoma

  1. Drug therapy:
    • Chemotherapy: Used to shrink the tumour and prevent it spreading. Chemotherapy may be systemic (intravenous) or local (intravitreal).
    • Immunotherapy: Medicines are used that stimulate the immune system to fight the cancer cells.
  2. Radiotherapy:
    • Brachytherapy: Placing radioactive seeds directly in the tumour for local treatment.
    • External beam radiotherapy: Radiation directed at the tumour to destroy the cancer cells.
  3. Surgery:
    • Enucleation: Removal of the eye in the case of large tumours or where there is a risk of spread.
    • Local resection: Removal of the tumour and some of the surrounding tissue.
  4. Laser therapy:
    • The use of a laser to destroy cancer cells in small, superficial tumours.

Advantages of treating retinoblastoma in Israel

  1. A high level of professionalism:
    • Israeli doctors have deep knowledge and many years of experience in treating retinoblastoma and other cancers.
  2. Modern equipment:
    • Clinics are equipped with advanced diagnostic and treatment devices, which allows highly accurate investigation and effective treatment.
  3. An individual approach:
    • Every patient is given an individual treatment plan that takes account of the nature of the condition and their general health.
  4. Innovative treatments:
    • The use of the most modern methods and medicines, including immunotherapy and photodynamic therapy.
  5. Comprehensive support:
    • Covers not only treatment of the underlying condition but also support for the patient's mental and physical wellbeing during treatment and rehabilitation.

Treatment of retinoblastoma in Israel gives patients access to high-quality medical care and considerably improves both the outlook and their quality of life.
